title: Guide to Pittsburgh Greek Food Festivals | 2025 Menus, Hours and Highlights | Visit Pittsburgh | When it comes to Greek food, it's not all Greek to me. We highlight the region's delicious summer season of Greek festivals taking place all across the city
text:
Insider's Guide to Pittsburgh Greek Food Festivals
When it comes to Greek food, it's not all Greek to me.
Names like spanakopita, moussaka, pastitsio speak to me just like the Sirens spoke to hungry sailors in the Odyssey. But without the evil overtones. Except for the Ouzo hangover and maybe the calories.
Greek food festival season normally runs from May-early Sept. each year in Pittsburgh at locations throughout the city and surrounding neighborhoods. To make life easy and maximize the time you can fill up on loukoumades (my personal favorite of bite-size donut balls drizzled with honey and cinnamon) here's your guide to the 2024 Greek food festival season.
Visiting this page after festival season? Hit up
Christo's
or
The Simple Greek
in Downtown Pittsburgh for these flavors year-round.
St. Nicholas Greek Food Festival
May 5-10, 2025 |
Menu
|
Order Online
The Greek food festival season officially kicks off at St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Cathedral in Oakland with a
weeklong food festival
with fantastic food and music until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays. It's easy to make a day of visiting this festival, too, with the Carnegie Museum of Art and Natural History, Cathedral of Learning and Schenley Park all just short walk from the festival. In just one bite you'll see why this festival has now been going on for 60+ years.
Pro Tip:
Head inside to find the dinners and a la carte options (their spanakopita and green beans yiahni are my two favorites) or go to the outdoor grill for gyros, Greek fries and salads.
All Saints Greek Food Festival
June 2-6, 2025
Greek dancing, live music, tons of vendors, and, oh yeah, the food is incredible too. Dolmathes (stuffed graped leaves), spanakopita (phyllo layers filled with spinach and feta cheese) and rizogalo (rice pudding) are just some of the many highlights at the
All Saints Greek Food Festival
! Follow their page on
Facebook
to learn more.
Holy Cross Greek Food Festival
June 9-13, 2025 | Online Ordering Available
Celebrating 52 years in 2025, the
Holy Cross Greek Food Festival
will transport you across the ocean from Mt. Lebanon without ever leaving your table. You'll find all the favorites here along with new items added to the menu all the time. Last year, the baklava blizzard, a frozen spin on the classic dessert, and a Greek loukaniko sausage were new fan favorites! Don't leave without watching the saganaki (flaming cheese) demo. Follow on
Facebook
for more info.
Annual Aliquippa Greek Food & Music Festival
June 12-14, 2025
Delivering mouthwatering Greek classics to hungry Aliquippans for almost 50 years,
Kimisis Tis Theotokou Greek Orthodox Church
is a great stop northwest of the city. Grab their lamb shank for a full dinner served with orzo, salad and pita or find ala carte bliss with some of the best moussaka (eggplant and ground beef in a cream sauce) and pastitsio (the same but with pasta instead of eggplant) you'll find anywhere!
Oakmont Greek Festival
June 27-29, 2025 | Online Ordering and Curbside Available
This Greek festival is so good I plan my summer travel around it so I never have to miss a year. My recommendation is to get to the
Oakmont Greek Festival
early and have a plan: one to the dessert line, one to the drinks and one to the main courses, then meet at the table and enjoy all together. Follow your nose to some of the best loukoumades (honey balls, be generous on the cinnamon) in the region and their signature chicken alexis glazed, with fruit and honey.
I mean, come on!
Annual Savor the Flavors of Greece
July 11, 2025
You only have one day to enjoy this parish festival from Saint Spyridon in Monessen, but just trust me that it's worth the drive. Unique favorites here include the psari plaki (baked cod presented Greek style), giouvetsi (orzo pasta and fresh veggies in a light tomato sauce) and gyros so good they have to sell them in their own tent! Follow them on
Facebook
for more info.
Holy Trinity Greek Food Festival (Ambridge)
July 15-19, 2025
Opa! The Holy Trinity Greek Food Festival in Ambridge has five days of food and fun along with a live band Friday and Saturday for a truly raucous celebration. Their website is still being updated, so more info on this one as we get closer! Follow on
Facebook
until then.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Holy Trinity (@htambridge)
East Pittsburgh Greek Fest
July 24-26, 2025
Sunny afternoons, cool nights, no problem. The
Annual East Pittsburgh Greek Fest
has a spacious indoor dining area at the Olympia Banquet Facility as well as an outdoor Grecian garden full of folk music and authentic dance that pairs perfectly with their gyros! Or, take a 1/2 pan of pastitsio or moussaka for Greek to-go.
Holy Trinity "Taste of Greece" Festival (Pittsburgh)
Aug. 28-31, 2025
Cap off an outstanding Greek food festival season in McCandless Township right at the
Taste of Greece
festival! Shuttles at nearby UPMC Passavant GREEN Lot will drop you off to this free festival where the favorites of souzoukakla (Greek baked meatballs in a tomato wine sauce), souvlaki (marinated pork grilled on a skewer) keep the locals and thousands of visitors coming back each year.
Special thanks to
Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church (Pittsburgh)
for compiling this free guide and helping get the word out about all of this incredible food, culture and fun!

title: Oakland | Visit Pittsburgh | Oakland is a must-visit for museum lovers and those looking for a quick escape from the bustling city.
text:
Oakland
A college hub that's so much more
A quick bus ride from anywhere in the city, Oakland is a must-visit for museum lovers and those looking for a quick escape from the bustling city.
5 Must-Do Activities in Oakland
1. Say Hi To Cathy
The tallest academic building in the Western Hemisphere, the University of Pittsburgh’s
Cathedral of Learning
– affectionately known as “Cathy” – sits in the middle of Pitt’s campus and serves as a token photo op moment. Once you step inside, you’ll be transported into a new, gothic-style world that will have you questioning if you’ve finally gotten your wizarding school invite. While there, take in the
Nationality Rooms
– Pitt’s community space where you're invited to experience your heritage in a space that's timeless and austere, yet dynamic and alive.
2. Enjoy the Garden Life
Explore the beauty and wonders of nature at
Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
, encompassing 15 acres including the historic 14-room glasshouse and 23 distinct gardens. Experience breathtaking seasonal flower shows, exclusive commissioned exhibits, immersive Tropical Forest, renowned orchid and bonsai collections, industry-leading sustainable architecture and green practices, delightful butterflies, fun family activities and much more. Discover why Phipps is a top destination for all ages, located just a few miles from downtown Pittsburgh in
Schenley Park
.
3. Take in the Great Outdoors
Speaking of,
Schenley Park
is a daily destination for university students, business people, and outdoor enthusiasts, while also hosting major annual events such as the
Vintage Grand Prix
and the Pittsburgh Race for the Cure. Visitors to Schenley Park can enjoy a light lunch at the Schenley Park Visitor Center, take a ride on the PNC carousel in Schenley Plaza, soak in the sunshine on the Arthur D. Hellman Lawn, relax on Flagstaff Hill, play a round at the Bob O’Connor Golf Course, head to the Schenley Oval Sportsplex for ice skating or summer sports, or take a dip in the swimming pool. And of course, the trails offer a refreshing and convenient escape from city noise and congestion.
4. Explore Two Museums in One
Explore two world-class museums with one ticket at
Carnegie Museums of Art and Natural History
! Located in the Oakland neighborhood, the museums provide an experience filled with culture, creativity, and exploration to all who visit. Carnegie Museum of Art, renowned for its collections of more than 100,00 objects, features a range of visual art, including painting, sculpture, decorative arts, design, and photography. Located within the same historic building, Carnegie Museum of Natural History is home to one of the country’s largest and most celebrated natural history collections featuring 22 million objects and specimens, ranging from real dinosaur fossils and dazzling gems and minerals to iconic wildlife dioramas.
5. Honor Our Troops
Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Hall & Museum
is a unique military memorial dedicated to honoring the men and women of all branches of service, from all generations and conflicts. Their vast collection of artifacts donated over the past 100 years gives Soldiers & Sailors Memorial & Museum a unique platform to interpret American military history by telling stories of individuals who served our country since the Civil War through our current era.

title: Allegheny City Center | Visit Pittsburgh | The Green Heart of the North Side
text:
Allegheny City Center
The Green Heart of the North Side
Allegheny City Central is a masterclass in urban character, defined by its lush landscapes and 19th-century elegance. At its core lies
Allegheny Commons Park
, Pittsburgh’s oldest park (est. 1867), which provides a serene, nature-filled escape with magnificent views of the downtown skyline. Surrounding this green sanctuary is an "arms wide open" community known for its extreme diversity and rich history.
The soul of this community is found within the
Mexican War Streets
, the city's first designated historic district. Originally platted in 1848, these streets were named to honor the battles and leaders of the Mexican-American War and today represent one of the most impeccably preserved Victorian-era neighborhoods in the United States. Walking these blocks is like stepping into a living museum, where original gas lamps and cobblestone alleys frame a diverse array of architectural styles, from grand Italianate estates to ornate Richardsonian Romanesque row houses.
5 Ways to Explore Allegheny City Center
1. Immerse Yourself in Allegheny Commons Park
Explore 80 acres of walking trails, bike paths, and the scenic
Lake Elizabeth
, or take advantage of the park's tennis, pickleball, and basketball courts.
2. Visit the Cultural Campus
Within a few blocks, you can engage with over 500 birds at the
National Aviary
, enjoy hands-on learning at the
Children’s Museum of Pittsburgh
, or see avant-garde art at the
Mattress Factory
.
3. Walk the Mexican War Streets & Sampsonia Way
Discover a transitional urban paradise of Victorian architecture and hidden gems like
City of Asylum
, which hosts writers living in exile, and the colorful nostalgia of
RandyLand
before walking into the art at the
Mattress Factory
.
4. Taste Global Flavors
Experience the neighborhood's diversity through its food, from
ShadoBeni’s
vegan Trinidadian dishes and
Pauline’s Caribbean Soul Cuisine
to the unique concepts at
Federal Galley
.
5. Join a Local Tradition
Participate in beloved community events such as the annual
Steel City Duck Derby
at Lake Elizabeth or the long-running
Pumpkinfest
.
Know Before You Go:
Street parking in Allegheny City Central is largely residential and strictly enforced. Always double-check for permit signs before you park to ensure your visit remains stress-free.

title: Allegheny West Neighborhood | Visit Pittsburgh | Part park, part college campus, all Pittsburgh spirit
text:
Allegheny West
Part park, part college campus, all Pittsburgh spirit
A quick ride on the “T” or a scenic walk from downtown Pittsburgh, Allegheny West is a must-visit for those who love the great outdoors and historic homes.
5 Must-Do Ways to Explore the Neighborhood
1. Relax at Allegheny Commons Park
If you’re looking for a chill day,
Allegheny Commons Park
is right in the heart of the North Side. Stop for a picnic, set up a hammock, or simply take a walk through; whatever you choose, it’ll make a nice reset during your trip.
2. See CCAC's Main Campus
The main campus of the Community College of Allegheny County calls West Allegheny home. With brick buildings tucked into their own little corner of the city, you'll be greeted with sweeping views and a great community - no pun intended.
3. Take In the Tiny Neighborhood
West Allegheny is proud to hold the title of Pittsburgh's smallest neighborhood, but you wouldn't know it from all it has to offer. From Allegheny Commons Park to some of the region's best locally-owned shops, you'll never be bored in this corner of the city.
4. Go Back in Time
West Allegheny is one of Pittsburgh's many historic districts, with historic homes scattered everywhere you look. Let the
official map of West Allegheny's historic homes
guide you down memory lane.
5. Visit the Toy Train Museum
The largest collection of antique American toy trains in the world is in on the outskirts of West Allegheny at the
Toy Train Museum
! Visit a magical world, surrounded by thousands of colorful toy trains made between 1860 and 1939 by companies like Lionel, American Flyer and Ives – many of them rolling merrily through miniature towns and countryside, tunnels and bridges. You'll want to plan your trip here in advance, as the Toy Train Museum is only open two days a year!

title: Brighton Heights | Visit Pittsburgh | Pittsburgh’s Hilltop Nature Escape
text:
Brighton Heights
Pittsburgh’s Hilltop Nature Escape
Perched beautifully on the scenic bluffs overlooking the Ohio River on Pittsburgh’s historic Northside, Brighton Heights blends quiet residential charm with immediate access to robust outdoor exploration.
Known for its commanding views and friendly, neighborhood atmosphere, this community offers the perfect vantage point to explore the outdoors without losing close proximity to Downtown Pittsburgh. Whether you are crossing a historic pedestrian bridge into deep wooded trails or enjoying a seasonal local festival, Brighton Heights stands out as one of the Northside's premier residential gems.
5 Must-See Things to Do in Brighton Heights
1. Cross the Davis Avenue Pedestrian Bridge to Riverview Park
Rebuilt to seamlessly reconnect the community, this sleek pedestrian and bike gateway provides direct, effortless entry from Brighton Heights right into the sprawling trail networks, mature woods, and hillsides of historic
Riverview Park
. It’s a premier route for local runners and cyclists seeking an immediate escape into nature.
2. Unwind at St. John's Green
This meticulously planned, three-acre inclusive park is a model for local sustainability. at
St. John's Green
, Wander along paved walking paths, admire the blooming native plants in the rain garden, or see what is growing in the volunteer-tended Brighton Heights Community Garden.
3. Reflect at Legion Memorial Park
Located at the central crossroads of Brighton Road, Shadeland Avenue, and Davis Avenue, this historic green space features mature canopy trees that transform beautifully with the seasons. At the heart of
Legion Memorial Park
stands a powerful 1922 bronze monument sculpted by Allen George Newman, offering a peaceful, contemplative spot right in the center of the neighborhood.
4. Catch a Neighborhood Summer Series Event
If you visit between May and October, head to the central park grounds to experience the true heart of the community. The monthly
Summer Series
gatherings assemble regional food trucks, hyper-local craft vendors, and live musical talent for an open-air celebration enjoyed by hundreds of residents.
5. Tour Historic Early 20th-Century Architecture
Brighton Heights is an architectural treasure trove featuring beautifully preserved brick and stone homes boasting ornate woodwork and timeless stained-glass windows. While beautiful to tour on foot any day of the year, the landmark
Annual Brighton Heights House and Garden Tour
opens up these residential masterpieces to the public every summer.

title: Central Northside Neighborhood | Visit Pittsburgh | Cobblestone streets and museums line this walkable neighborhood
text:
Central Northside
Cobblestone streets and museums line this walkable neighborhood
A quick ride on the “T” or a scenic walk from downtown Pittsburgh, Central Northside plays home to museums, cobblestone streets, mom and pop shops, and beautiful outdoor spaces.
5 Must-Do Ways to Explore the Neighborhood
1. Immerse Yourself in The Mattress Factory
Mattress Factory Museum of Contemporary Art
has pioneered the development of alternative art forms through site-specific installations, video and performance art. It is nationally and internationally recognized as a leader in site-specific, contemporary art and is notorious for pushing the boundaries of both artist and viewer. The unparalleled support that artists receive from the Mattress Factory, while working in residence, often results in the production of extraordinary artwork that propels the artist’s career and significantly impacts the field of contemporary art.
2. Walk Through the Mexican War Streets
No matter the weather, a walk through the
Mexican War Streets
is a must. Take in the vibrancy of Pittsburgh’s most colorful homes with a coffee from Commonplace Coffee in hand.
3. Experience Color Like Never Before at Randyland
When we say this is a Pittsburgh staple, we mean it.
Randyland
is an open air museum that is often considered to be the city's most colorful spot, all built by the creative vision of artist Randy Gilson.
4. Go Back in Time at the George Washington Ferris House
Experience a little history at the
George Washington Ferris House
, tucked away in Central Northside. It was once the home of George Washington Gale Ferris Jr., who designed and constructed the original Ferris Wheel for the World's Columbian Exposition of 1893.
5. Support Local Artists at City of Asylum
City of Asylum
creates a thriving community for writers, readers and neighbors. Its cultural center, Alphabet City, features cultural events and a bookstore showcasing literature in translation.

title: East Allegheny Neighborhood | Visit Pittsburgh | Also known as Pittsburgh's Deutschtown!
text:
East Allegheny
Also known as Pittsburgh's Deutschtown!
A quick ride on the “T” or a scenic walk from downtown Pittsburgh, East Allegheny is a must-visit that's situated between the trees and trails of Allegheny Commons Park and the traffic of Interstate 279.
5 Must-Do Ways to Explore the Neighborhood
1. Visit Photo Antiquities Museum of Photographic History
View archives of Pittsburgh, Civil War and Native American photographic images from all over the world at
Photo Antiquities Museum of Photographic History
. The museum's collection includes Daguerreotypes, Ambrotypes, Tintypes, Lantern Slides, Stereo Views and paper process.
2. See a Show at The Government Center
One part concert venue, one part record store, one part coffee shop, and one part bar - what else could you want in one place?
The Government Center
is a place where anyone can hang out and talk about music, and it's open to the needs of the community.
3. Break Out the Banjos
Ff you happen to find yourself in Deutschtown on a Wednesday evening after 8:00, you might want to experience the free sing-a-long known as "Banjo Night" at the
Elks Lodge #339
.
4. Grab a Brew at Allegheny City Brewing
Deutschtown has gotten into the craft beer craze as well.
Allegheny City Brewing
was opened in 2016 by a trio who returned to Pittsburgh following several years in Colorado. Their tap room is a tribute to the city of Allegheny, which was the name of Pittsburgh's North Side before it was annexed in 1907, and the revolving list of beers includes Nova Gose, Graham Cracker Porter and Grapefruit Imperial IPA.
5. Dance the Day Away at Northside Music Festival
Held every summer,
Northside Music Festival
features dozens of bands performing across indoor and outdoor venues during this signature three-day event. The free festival also includes art vendors and more than 20 food trucks. This non-profit, all-volunteer music festival is one of Pittsburgh’s signature summer events and a great way to support and promote local bands and bring the Northside community together.

text:
Pittsburgh’s North Shore and North Side
The North Shore, Central Northside, Allegheny Center, East Allegheny, and Allegheny West
A quick ride on the “T” or a scenic walk from downtown Pittsburgh, the North Shore and North Side are must-visits for sports enthusiasts, museum lovers and everyone in between.
The North Shore is a hub for most things Pittsburgh sports, while the North Side features gorgeous parks and colorful streets, but both are home to some of the city’s most popular museums.
5 Must-Do Ways to Explore the Neighborhood
1. Explore the Mexican War Streets
No matter the weather, a walk through the
Mexican War Streets
is a must. Take in the vibrancy of Pittsburgh’s most colorful homes with a coffee from
Commonplace Coffee
in hand. You can also stop at a variety of museums in the area, like
The Mattress Factory
,
Randyland
, and the
National Aviary
.
2. Get There in Style
There are plenty of ways to get to the North Shore, but we highly recommend either walking or
biking
across a bridge from Downtown. There are plenty to choose from that will spit you out wherever you want to go along the Allegheny River. Bonus points if there’s a
Pittsburgh
Pirates
game, because then the iconic
Roberto Clemente Bridge
is shut down and you can walk on its street.
3. Relax at Allegheny Commons Park
If you’re looking for a chill day,
Allegheny Commons Park
is right in the heart of the North Side. Stop for a picnic, set up a hammock, or simply take a walk through; whatever you choose, it’ll make a nice reset during your trip.
4. Catch a Game
Of course, the North Shore’s most iconic features are its stadiums. This neighborhood is home to both the
Pittsburgh Steelers
(
Acrisure Stadium
) and the
Pittsburgh Pirates
(
PNC Park
), as well as the
Pitt Panthers
football team. Experience the City of Champions for yourself on the North Shore no matter the season, and make sure to bring your
Terrible Towel
!
5. Visit a Museum
As mentioned, the North Shore and North Side are home to several museums that cater to whatever your niche.
Into contemporary art and not afraid to step out of your comfort zone? Head to
The Mattress Factory
,
Randyland
,
Museum of Illusions
, or the
Andy Warhol Museum
. Are you a diehard sports fan? Visit the
Steelers Hall of Honor Museum
inside
Acrisure Stadium
and track down the many plaques in the area showcasing some of the city’s most legendary moments on the field. Looking for something a little more practical. Check out the
Kamin Science Center
, recently named
USA Today
’s third best science museum in the country! And what about the kids? The
Children’s Museum of Pittsburgh and MuseumLab
is also in the North Side, and was recently voted the best children’s museum in the United States by USA Today!

title: Troy Hill | Visit Pittsburgh | Troy Hill is a must-visit for art lovers and those looking for a quick escape from the bustling city.
text:
Troy Hill
Just one of Pittsburgh's many "Hill" neighborhoods
A quick ride on the “T” or a scenic walk from downtown Pittsburgh or the Strip District, Troy Hill is a must-visit for art lovers and those looking for a quick escape from the bustling city.
5 Must-Do Activities in Troy Hill
1. Journey Through Hidden Art Houses
Discover the
Troy Hill Art Houses
, one of Pittsburgh’s biggest hidden gems. While these homes may look normal from the outside, the insides have been renovated into a total structure art piece. From the incredible lighthouse-within-a-house of the Darkhouse Lighthouse, photography-inspired Kunzhaus and inspired use of everyday objects in La Hütte Royal, find the house that calls to you!
2. See One of America's Steepest Streets
Take in the sights from
Rialto Street,
which features one of the steepest (and narrowest) roads in the city accompanied by nearly 500 feet of stairs to reach the heart of the Troy Hill neighborhood.
3. Take the Stairs
Enjoy this walker’s paradise neighborhood by climbing staircases connecting side streets, sometimes jutting between houses and other times ending in parks or right by a brewery. There's even a self-guided walking tour you can take that highlights eight staircases including Rialto.
4. Step Back Through Pittsburgh's History Books
Stop in to
Penn Brewery
, Pittsburgh’s oldest craft brewery dating back all the way to 1986. If you love German brews, start with their flagship Penn Pilsner or Penn Dark (my personal fave) or look for specialty styles like their pumpkin roll or Oktoberfest depending on when you visit. Their beautiful outdoor biergarten is the perfect place to sip and enjoy their menu of both German and Pittsburgh favorites from potato pancakes and pork schnitzel to pierogi and French fries on your salad.
5. Appreciate Ancient Relics
Churches dot the landscape of Troy Hill, but one in particular is a must-see for anyone interested in religion or history.
St. Anthony's Chapel
contains more than 5,000 relics of the Roman Catholic faith including the skulls of martyred saints, fragments of the cross that Jesus was crucified on, a piece of Mary's veil and bones from all 12 of Jesus' disciples.

title: Bloomfield | Visit Pittsburgh | Welcome to Pittsburgh’s "Little Italy."
text:
Bloomfield
Welcome to Pittsburgh’s "Little Italy."
Bloomfield is a welcoming, deeply rooted neighborhood where multi-generational heritage blends seamlessly with modern community charm. Hugging the bustling commercial strip of Liberty Avenue, Bloomfield is famous for its old-world Italian markets, towering classic neon signs, and friendly, independent business owners. From historic scratch bakeries and legendary hardwood grills to progressive bookstores and highly acclaimed new Scandinavian bistros, Bloomfield offers a rich, comforting experience defined by immense local pride and time-honored traditions.
5 Must-See Experiences in Bloomfield
1. Bite into a Legendary Tessaro's Burger
Pull up a chair at this iconic Pittsburgh landmark to enjoy a thick, juicy hamburger ground fresh daily by an in-house butcher and seared over a custom iron grill fueled entirely by Pennsylvania hardwood.
2. Shop the Historic Markets of Little Italy
Take a sensory stroll through multi-generational staples like
Bloomfield Groceria
and
Merante's
, where you can pick up handmade ravioli, fresh gnocchi, imported olive oils, and authentic Italian housewares.
3. Get Lost in White Whale Bookstore
Browse the beautifully curated shelves of this independent, family-owned literary haven that serves as a vital community space, complete with a cozy café serving local coffee and craft beers.
4. Catch a Bocce Game under the Bridge
Walk down toward the
Bloomfield Bridge
next to the public park on a warm evening to watch locals gather for lively matches on the public bocce courts, keeping a classic neighborhood tradition alive.
5. Savor an Authentic Cannoli at Paddy Cake Bakery
Satisfy your sweet tooth at this traditional scratch bakery along Liberty Avenue, a mandatory neighborhood stop famous for its fresh breads, oversized cookies, and crisp, perfectly piped cannoli.
Pro Tip: Cross the Avenue for Contemporary Arts
Bloomfield's deep historic roots make it a masterclass in local tradition, but it sits directly adjacent to one of the city's most progressive cultural districts. When you reach the western end of Liberty Avenue near West Penn Hospital, simply walk north down 48th Street for less than five minutes. You'll land right on Penn Avenue, instantly connecting you to a completely different neighborhood vibe.
Looking to experience this neighboring creative powerhouse? Head over to our
Garfield Neighborhood Hub
to explore local galleries and maker scene.

text:
Central Lawrenceville
Central Lawrenceville is right in the middle of a cluster of some of the most beloved neighborhoods in Pittsburgh.
A quick drive or a scenic bike ride from downtown Pittsburgh, Central Lawrenceville is a must-visit for shoppers and those looking for a quick escape from the bustling city.
5 Must-Do Activities in Central Lawrenceville
1. Enjoy the Scenery at Allegheny Cemetery
We know what you're thinking, but trust us when we say this is a cemetery you have to see. Nestled in the middle of Lawrenceville, Allegheny Cemetery is a place that will make you forget you were ever in a city to begin with. Beautiful mausoleums, statues, and gravestones greet you as you journey through sprawling hills. We recommend bringing a blanket and a book, especially during the autumn months.
2. Create Your Perfect Candle at Mix Candle Co.
It's so hard to find the perfect candle, but luckily Central Lawrenceville has a place where you can make your own perfect scent.
Mix Candle Co.
provides dozens of scents that you can mix and match to create your dream candle. Experts walk you through what vibe your looking for and combinations that will get you there. The best part - you can usually pick up your candle that same day, so you can kill time while waiting by shopping and grabbing a bite to eat nearby.
3. Grab Your Next Read at Pittsburgh's Romance-Only Bookstores
With a renewed surge of reading romance, Pittsburgh has answered the call. Enter The Shelf Love Society and Passionate Pages, Pittsburgh's romance-exclusive bookstores. Both have a curated selection of bestsellers, local authors, and everything in between, so you'll walk out with one - or several - new additions to your to-be-read pile. The best part - both are located along Butler Street!
4. Pick Your Meal at Lawrence Hall
It's the age old question - what do you want to eat? For those who just can't make up your mind, you won't have to at
Lawrence Hall
. This food hall has plenty of diverse spots that will satisfy even the pickiest of eaters.
5. See a Show at Thunderbird Cafe and Music Hall
Pittsburgh is packed with music venues, and one of our hidden gems is right in Central Lawrenceville. Thunderbird Cafe and Music Hall is a bi-level bar and live music venue that features national and local bands plus bar food and craft brews.

Lower Lawrenceville is just the beginning of a cluster of some of the most beloved neighborhoods in Pittsburgh.

5 Must-Do Activities in Lower Lawrenceville
1. Walk Through History at The Clemente Museum
Sports fans, this one is for you.
The Clemente Museum
in Lower Lawrenceville is an homage to Pittsburgh Pirates legend Roberto Clemente. Located in historic Engine House 25, it houses largest collection of Roberto Clemente memorabilia in the world
2. Treat Yourself at Arsenal Cider House
Usually we'd say save the cider for fall, but
Arsenal Cider House & Wine Cellar
is a perfect spot no matter the season or weather. With award-winning ciders and meads, you'll be blown away by this small-batch, independently-crafted cider. And if cider isn't your thing, you'll be delighted at other options on the menu.
3. Shop and Eat Along Butler Street
Butler Street in Lawrenceville is one of Pittsburgh's most eclectic roadways, with stores that will make you look twice while you window shop. In Lower Lawrenceville, we recommend stopping at Gemini Vintage, Umami, Morcilla, and
Burghers Brewing Company
, just to name a few.
4. Go Rock Climbing at Iron City Boulders
We love reimagined spaces, and one of Pittsburgh's best examples is
The Church Brew Works
. It's exactly how it sounds - an old church that's been redesigned into a brewing company! The structure is the same as it's always been, so prepare to swoon over the stained glass windows and rustic feel while sipping on your new favorite drinks.
5. Relax at Arsenal Park
Days in Lawrenceville can be long. We get it - there's just so much to do! That's why we recommend taking a breather at Arsenal Park, right at the border between Lower Lawrenceville and Central Lawrenceville. Bonus points if you pick up lunch on Butler Street to enjoy while you recharge.

Contemporary Craft
engages the public in creative experiences through craft. title: Regent Square | Visit Pittsburgh | A Tree-Lined Neighborhood Defined by Small-Town Charm
text:
Regent Square
A Tree-Lined Neighborhood Defined by Small-Town Charm
Tucked along the eastern edge of Frick Park, Regent Square is one of Pittsburgh’s most walkable neighborhood gems, with leafy streets, independent shops, and an easygoing village feel. Around South Braddock and Trenton Avenues, you’ll find the kind of local spots residents love to share: cozy cafés, curated bookstores, neighborhood pubs, handcrafted goods, and quick access to some of the city’s best wooded trails. Come for a hike, stay for a slow stroll down historic brick streets, and you’ll see why this East End neighborhood feels like a friendly escape just minutes from downtown Pittsburgh.
5 Ways to Explore Regent Square
1. Step Directly from Main Street to Forest Trails
Few places in the city let you transition so seamlessly from a boutique coffee shop to deep forest trails. As a primary gateway to the 644-acre
Frick Park
, Regent Square lets you start your morning with a stroll along Nine Mile Run or a brisk hike under lush forest canopies, all just steps from South Braddock Avenue.
2. Experience an Independent, Neighbor-Driven Dining Scene
Regent Square’s culinary offerings are proudly local and packed with character. Grab a casual bite and pick out a craft brew from the famous
"Beer Cave"
at
D’s Six Pax & Dogz
, or gather for dinner and creative cocktails in the Pacific Northwest-inspired dining room at
Hemlock House
. From cozy Italian bistros to neighborhood taverns, every spot feels like a local secret.
3. Stroll & Shop South Braddock and Trenton Avenues
The tree-lined corridors along South Braddock and Trenton Avenues host an eclectic collection of independent shops. You can pick up fresh sourdough croissants at
Madeline’s Bakery
, grab an espresso at
Biddle's Escape
, discover your next read at
Stay Gold Books
, or browse handcrafted home goods at
Workshop PGH
. Outdoor enthusiasts can also drop into
3 Rivers Outdoor Co.
for gear, apparel, and community events.
4. Discover Historic Streetscapes & Architecture
Take a self-guided walking tour down the neighborhood’s historic brick-paved side streets. The quiet, shaded blocks are lined with beautifully preserved early 20th-century American Foursquares, Craftsman bungalows, and welcoming front porches that showcase quintessential East End neighborhood character.
5. Experience Iconic Community Festivals
Plan your trip around one of the neighborhood’s annual gatherings. Experience the excitement of the
Run Around the Square
(RATS) 5K and dog walk every August, hunt for vintage treasures at the multi-block Annual Yard Sale in the spring, or enjoy live music and local food vendors during the autumn Fall Festival.

title: Squirrel Hill Pittsburgh Neighborhood | Visit Pittsburgh | Visit Pittsburgh | Explore Squirrel Hill Pittsburgh where there's a variety of ethnic food and two large parks to walk off whatever kind of meal you decide on.
text:
Squirrel Hill
Pittsburgh’s Vibrant Urban Village
Welcome to Squirrel Hill, the neighborhood so legendary it inspired Mr. Rogers himself. As one of the most culturally diverse and welcoming corners of Pittsburgh, this is a place where "relaxed luxury meets modern elegance". Whether you're a foodie, an outdoor adventurer, or a history buff, Squirrel Hill offers a unique blend of international flavor and historic charm that makes every visitor feel like a local.
Historically, the neighborhood is a treasure trove of Pittsburgh stories. It's home to the
Neill Log House
, the oldest restored log house in the area. It's also the stomping grounds of modern icons like
Mac Miller
and
Wiz Khalifa
. From the bustling business districts to the quiet, tree-lined residential streets, Squirrel Hill is a walker’s paradise designed for exploration.
5 Must-Do Ways to Explore the Neighborhood
1. Take the "Great Pizza Debate" Challenge
In Squirrel Hill, your pizza choice is a local tradition. Two legends,
Mineo’s Pizza House
(2128 Murray Ave) and
Aiello’s Pizza
(2112 Murray Ave), have sat just a block apart for decades. Mineo’s is famous for its mountain of hand-grated cheese, while Aiello’s is the go-to for a classic, crispy crust.
Pro Tip:
Grab a slice from both and decide for yourself which reigns supreme!
2. Walk in the Footsteps of Legends
Pay homage to the neighborhood’s most famous neighbors. Visit
Blue Slide Park
(part of Frick Park), which served as the namesake for
Mac Miller’s
debut album, or walk past
Taylor Allderdice High School
, the alma mater of both Miller and
Wiz Khalifa
. Of course, no visit is complete without a nod to
Mister Rogers
himself, Fred Rogers; Squirrel Hill was his longtime home, and the community still embodies his "won't you be my neighbor" spirit.
3. Get Active in Pittsburgh’s "Green Heart"
Squirrel Hill is bordered by three of the city’s most spectacular parks:
Schenley
,
Frick
, and
Mellon
. You can hike the wooded trails of Frick Park, visit the
Frick Environmental Center
for a sensory garden experience, or tee off at the
Bob O’Connor Golf Course
(5370 Schenley Dr) the only golf course located within Pittsburgh city limits.
4. Explore International Cuisine and Local Favorites
Savor the city’s largest concentrated selection of global cuisine along Forbes and Murray Avenues. Experience the James Beard-nominated heat of
Chengdu Gourmet
and the hand-pulled ribbons at
Amazing Dumplings
, or dive into the neighborhood's deep Jewish roots with a fresh-boiled bagel from
Pigeon Bagels
and a "Honey Bunny Latte" at
Bunny Bakes
. Afterward, cool down with a specialty brew in the Bubble Tea District, where you'll find authentic matcha and Taiwanese tea spots tucked between historic kosher markets.
5. Walk the Timeline of History
Discover a piece of the 1700s tucked away during a stroll through Schenley Park.
The Neill Log House
(E Circuit Rd) is the oldest restored log house in the area and stands as a quiet reminder of the neighborhood's frontier past. Then, fast forward to the 20th century at one of the oldest and most storied cinemas in Pittsburgh. Since opening its doors in 1922,
The Manor
has evolved from a silent film house into a sophisticated destination for indie and foreign films.

title: Must-Attend Events & Festivals: North Shore & North Side | Visit Pittsburgh | Discover the many things to do in Pittsburgh PA. Enjoy exciting Pittsburgh tourism activities, take in scenic views, and eat at award-winning restaurants.
text:
Must-Attend Events & Festivals: North Shore & North Side
An iconic Pittsburgh location, the North Shore and North Side come alive year-round with must-attend events and festivals. Timing your visit to coincide with these signature events offers a chance to see the riverfront at its most energetic and vibrant.
Annual Events & Festivals
DICK’S Sporting Goods Pittsburgh Marathon
| Various
One of the city's most electric weekends, where the North Shore takes part of the celebration and the energy is concentrated at the finish line in the heart of the Golden Triangle. The course winds through several diverse neighborhoods before culminating Downtown with live music, "cheer stations," and a massive street party atmosphere for runners and spectators alike.
The Annual Mexican War Streets Yard Sale
| 1201 Sherman Ave.
On the first breath of summer in June, the streets will open their secrets. Follow the brick paths where history hums, and you’ll find treasures waiting in plain sight. Look for the houses with open doors—those are the ones ready to trade stories. If you hear laughter echoing between the rowhomes, you’re close. If you smell old books and fresh coffee, you’re there. The annual gathering is coming… and the Mexican War Streets are ready to reveal what they’ve been keeping.
Northside Music Festival
| 511 Foreland St.
The Northside Music Festival encompasses a huge swath of this booming neighborhood. Two main outdoor stages at Allegheny Commons Park and on Foreland & Middle's intersection anchor the festival, with additional venues at popular businesses on the Northside including The Government Center, Allegheny City Brewing, Allegheny Elks Lodge and Fat Cat for more live music.
Picklesburgh
| Pittsburgh's Sister Bridges
Voted the #1 specialty food festival in the country, this "only-in-Pittsburgh" experience takes over the Sister Bridges (Roberto Clemente and Andy Warhol). Famous for its giant 35-foot flying Heinz pickle balloon, the event offers pickle-themed cocktails, live music, and the fan-favorite pickle juice drinking contest.
America’s Mile
| North Shore
A spectacular race event open to all, set against Pittsburgh's breathtaking North Shore.
Kickoff and Rib Festival
| Acrisure Stadium
The Kickoff and Rib Festival was started in 1990 at Three Rivers Stadium. Much like today’s event, it featured concerts by national artists, national rib vendors, games and more.

title: 26 Things to Do While in Town for the 2026 NFL Draft | Visit Pittsburgh | Pittsburgh's North Shore and Downtown are going to be all things NFL Draft from April 23-25, 2026, but other areas of the city are also coming alive too.
text:
26 Things to Do While in Town for the 2026 NFL Draft
Pittsburgh's North Shore and Downtown are going to be all things NFL Draft from April 23-25, 2026, but other areas of the city are also coming alive in celebration.
With so much to see and do, we've compiled a list of the top 26 things you need to do in Pittsburgh while you're in town for the
2026 NFL Draft
.
1. Visit Arts Landing
Arts Landing, Downtown Pittsburgh's newest outdoor space, will soft open for the 2026 NFL Draft with an activation through the University of Pittsburgh. This area has transformed over the past year since groundbreaking, going from a parking lot to a gorgeous civic space that centers the Allegheny River and two of the Three Sisters Bridges, welcoming pedestrians from multiple entrances. The Draft is your chance to enjoy the space before its grand opening in June with
Three Rivers Arts Festival.
Credit
|
Renderings by Field Operations
Credit
|
Renderings by Field Operations
2. Adventure in the
North Side
With the main footprint of the Draft happening along Pittsburgh's Allegheny River, it's easy to take a quick walk both outside of the Draft Experience to other parts of the North Shore and up to the North Side and experience one of the city's most popular neighborhoods. Take in some of our beloved museums, like the
Kamin Science Center
(where you can watch
The Football Town
, an NFL Films project about Western Pennsylvania's ties to the sport),
Mattress Factory Museum of Contemporary Art
,
National Aviary
(open Saturday, April 25),
Children's Museum of Pittsburgh and MuseumLab
,
Moonshot Museum
,
Museum of Illusions
,
Andy Warhol Museum
,
Bicycle Heaven Museum
, and Randyland. Allegheny Commons Park is a short walk away if you want a break from the action, and the
'Burgh Bits & Bites
Allegheny North Side Food Tour will take you around to the area's best spots for some grub.
Click here
for more to do in Pittsburgh's North Shore and North Side.
Please note, some businesses may have limited hours during the Draft.
Credit
|
Julie Kahlbaugh
Credit
|
Julie Kahlbaugh
3. Enjoy the
Spring Weather
Pittsburgh is proud of experience all four seasons year-round, and the end of April is when the sun starts to truly shine. It's the perfect time of year to take in Pittsburgh's great outdoors without it being too scorching outside. Go on a
walk
with
Free Pittsburgh Walking Tours
, catch our unique redbud trees in peak bloom, grab a
bike
from
POGOH Bikeshare
stations around the city and enjoy a ride, whether on your own or during the
Draft Day Ride with the Pittsburgh Major Taylor Cycling Club and Black Girls Do Bike: Pittsburgh
.
4. Catch a Show
There's so much entertainment happening around the city during the Draft that you'll have a hard time picking which shows to go to. On Draft Eve, you can catch
PicksBURGH Music Edition
, a music crawl taking over a variety of venues in several neighborhoods throughout the city featuring music for all types of crowds. Then, throughout the week,
several venues throughout the city are hosting national names
, like Ice Spice, Steve Aoki, Nelly, and 2 Chainz, just to name a few. And of course, there will be
entertainment at the Draft Theater
, with Pittsburgh-area natives Wiz Khalifa and Bret Michaels are headlining a show on Friday, April 24, while Kane Brown is headlining a show on Saturday, April 25.
5. Get Your Sports Gear in the Strip District
A quick walk from Downtown, the Strip District is one of Pittsburgh's best neighborhoods to grab some sports gear. Several pop up shops and beloved mainstays line the streets, selling anything you need from cheesy t-shirts to staples like
Terrible Towels
. While you're in the area, stop by the original
Primanti Brother's
- one of Pittsburgh's most recognizable restaurants - and grab a bite, or stop by
The Terminal
for a variety of bites and things to do between picks.
6. Visit a Sports Museum
If you're here for the Draft, it's safe to say you're a sports fan. Luckily for you, Pittsburgh is the
City of Champions
and has several museums dedicated specifically to sports. The
Heinz History Center
- recently named the
best history museum in the country by USA Today
for the third year in a row - is home to the Franco Harris Sports Museum, which tells the stories of Pittsburghers who became champions and champions who became Pittsburghers. The History Center is also premiering a special Draft exhibition during the week, so catch it before it's gone!
The
Steelers Hall of Honor Museum
inside Acrisure Stadium is a must-visit for football fans. Right in the heart of the Draft footprint, the expansive displays truly capture the heart of one of the NFL's most stories franchises. With everything going on, it might be hard to get in, but trust us when we say it's worth a trip back.
And for baseball fans,
The Clemente Museum
is in Lawrenceville, a short distance from the Heinz History Center in the Strip District. Housed in a historic firehouse, the Clemente Museum is hosts the world’s largest exhibited collection of baseball artifacts, works of art, literature, photographs, memorabilia, and related materials which focus on Roberto Clemente, his teammates, his personal life, and his humanitarian causes.
Pictured
|
Western PA Sports Museum at the Heinz History Center
Credit
|
Jody Mader
Pictured
|
Western PA Sports Museum at the Heinz History Center
Credit
|
Jody Mader
7. Tour Pittsburgh's
Sports Heritage Trail
Pittsburgh is the City of Champions when it comes to our teams, but it's also true when it comes to the athletes who were born and raised here. As such, throughout the city, you can find several markers and landmarks that signify important moments in our sports history. From the location of the Immaculate Reception to the marker of the first professional football game, you'll learn something new wherever you go along the trail.
Pictured
|
Immaculate Reception monument - a holy pilgrimage for any non-Raiders football fan
Pictured
|
Immaculate Reception monument - a holy pilgrimage for any non-Raiders football fan
8. Take an Incline to Mt. Washington
A Pittsburgh trip isn't complete without a trip to Mt. Washington. And the best way to get there is up either the
Monongahela Incline
or
Duquesne Incline
. Both offer exceptional views of the city skyline and Acrisure Stadium, and the Monongahela Incline is free to use during the Draft thanks to Sheetz!
9. Discover
Market Square
's New Look
Market Square, in the heart of Downtown Pittsburgh, has been under renovations for the past few months. The Draft is the first chance the public will have to enjoy its new features and amenities, all with a Draft activation that will tie the grand opening together! With live music, themed events, and more, you won't want to miss out on this hub for Draft entertainment.
10. Ride on the
Gateway Clipper
Another Pittsburgh staple made free during the Draft, the Gateway Clipper can normally be found giving tours along Pittsburgh's three rivers. During the Draft, the fleet with be used to transport fans between the two main areas of the campus - North Shore and
Point State Park
. You can also take it from Station Square to
PNC Park
or vice versa, both of which are outside of the Draft Experience footprint.
11. Experience Draft Activities at
Point State Park
Speaking of, Point State Park also experienced renovations and will be ready to go for the Draft. It's fitting, because it's part of the main Draft footprint and will be where the red carpet is held. There will also be plenty of Draft activations among the greenery, including a sight-seeing space hosted by the
Steelers
and more.
12. Watch the Draft from a Local
Sports Bar
Watching the Draft in the heart of the footprint is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, but if you'd like to rest, there's no shame in watching it from the comfort of a barstool. Luckily, Pittsburgh is riddled with sports bars around every corner. Post up at places like
Mike's Beer Bar
,
Tom's Watch Bar
,
Redbeard's
,
Primanti's
, Capo's, or
Title 9
and catch all the action with a cold beer in hand and bar bites in your stomach.
13. Support
Pittsburgh's Newest Businesses
Pittsburgh is a city on the rise, and we're always welcoming new businesses into our 90 neighborhoods. Already in 2026, we have over a dozen new businesses that are already so beloved in our community, From candle making spaces and coffee shops to restaurants and gift shops, you'll find whatever you're looking for among our new storefronts.
Credit
|
VisitPITTSBURGH
Credit
|
VisitPITTSBURGH
14. Take Pittsburgh Home with You
Speaking of shopping local, there are some Pittsburgh staples that you'll definitely want to snag from souvenirs from. Stop by
love, Pittsburgh
for a more artsy feel, or go to
Steel City
for something a little more gritty. Whatever your style, you'll find something to take home with you.
15. Go on a Museum Crawl
We mentioned the museums that are in Pittsburgh's North Side and the sports museums, but there are more scattered throughout our 90 neighborhoods. The
Carnegie Museum of Art and Natural History
are located in the heart of Oakland and the University of Pittsburgh's campus. Also in Oakland are
Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Hall & Museum
and
Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
. You won't have to go far from Oakland to find
The Frick Museum
, and if you didn't check out the rest of the
Heinz History Center
while visiting the Franco Harris Sports Museum, don't miss it.
16. Taste the Flavors of Pittsburgh
Pittsburgh is Primanti's, but we're also pierogis, chipped ham, and
pączki
. And those are just our every day flavors. We're proud of have world-renowned restaurants and chefs in our community, serving up dishes that will make your tastebuds explode with flavor and remind you of grandma's home cooking all in one bite. Try FET-FISK, Apteka, Pusadee's Garden, and
Balvanera
just to start.
Pictured
|
Apteka
Credit
|
Ben Filio
Pictured
|
Apteka
Credit
|
Ben Filio
17. Visit Where Famous Athletes have Called Home
Dozens of legendary athletes grew up in our backyard, so why not take the time to visit their old neighborhoods while you're in town. Just to name a few:
Bill Cowher was born in Crafton
Aaron Donald was born in Lincoln-Lemington-Belmar
Damar Hamlin was born in McKees Rocks
Joe Namath was born in Beaver Falls
Arnold Palmer was born in Latrobe
Dan Marino was born in South Oakland
Jim Kelly was born in Pittsburgh and grew up in East Brady
Joe Montana was born in New Eagle
Pat McAfee was born in Plum
Mike Ditka was born in Carnegie
Tony Dorsett was born in Rochester and grew up in Aliquippa
More famous Pittsburghers
18. Experience
PicksBURGH
For the Draft, Pittsburgh is becoming PicksBURGH - featuring a collection of events designed to hype you up during the week. Run P3R's
Draft Day 5K
, tour Draft Eve's
Music Crawl
, and more!
19. Visit Pittsburgh's #1 Giraffe Pick
Perfect for families, the
Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium
is in Highland Park - just a few miles away from Downtown. And with the NFL Draft, the zoo decided to hop in on the fun by hosting the #1 giraffe pick...get it? The zoo has been continuously revamped over the past few years, with renovations and new exhibits coming to life before our eyes. Don't miss out on this family-friendly event throughout the weekend!
20. Find Your Favorite Local Brew or Craft Cocktail
Pittsburgh is full of breweries and cocktail bars just waiting for you to try their specialties. No matter your preference, you need to try an IC Light for starters. But after that, it's time to expand your flavor palate. For beer lovers, check out
Southern Tier Brewery
, East End Brewing, Trace Brewing, Grist House, and Allegheny City Brewing, just to name a few. If you prefer craft cocktails, we recommend
Wigle Whiskey
, Margaux, Emerson's,
William Omni
's speakeasy, Bar Botanica, and Commerce.
Credit
|
Lauren Petrilla
Credit
|
Lauren Petrilla
21. Explore Another Pittsburgh Neighborhood
In and around the Draft footprint, you'll be spending most of your time Downtown and on the North Shore. But during your downtime before or after the Draft, our other neighborhoods are just waiting to be discovered.
Mount Washington
is filled with local shops that you can visit after taking in a gorgeous view of our skyline,
Lawrenceville
is walkable and houses a diverse array of cuisine,
Squirrel Hill
is a coffee and tea lover's paradise, and South Side is the spot to bee if you want to grab a beer.
Learn more about all 90 of our neighborhoods
22. Go on a World Tour from Pittsburgh
You came to Pittsburgh, and now it's time to immerse yourself in the rest of the world. The University of Pittsburgh's Cathedral of Learning - the tallest academic building in the Western hemisphere - is home to the
Nationality Rooms
, which act as a community space where you're invited to experience your heritage in a space that's timeless and austere, yet dynamic and alive. Immerse yourself in the culture of Poland, Japan, Sweden, and more right in our backyard.
23. Ride a Roller Coaster or Two
The Draft has perfect timing, because
Kennywood Amusement Park
opens for the season on April 18. That means that when you're in town, you can take a short drive to West Mifflin and experience the park before it gets busier this summer. Ride the Steel Curtain and Phantom's Revenge, take a picture in front of the iconic tunnel, and don't forget to grab some Potato Patch fries!
24. Discover Pittsburgh's Hidden Gems
We've told you so many things you can do when you're here, yet there's still more to be discovered. Pittsburgh has something for everyone hidden around every corner, and luckily, we did the looking for you. Check out our list of
Pittsburgh's best kept secrets.
25. Extend Your Trip
Do you really have to go? The Draft isn't even the start of what we have to offer in the Steel City. With the
Pittsburgh Pirates
season starting up and games at PNC Park the weekend before the Draft, there's no reason you can't come to town early or stay late. Plus, the
Pittsburgh Penguins
are in the playoffs for the first time in a few years, and the defending champion Pittsburgh
Riverhounds
are back in action at
Highmark Stadium
. Couple those with the
59th Carnegie International
kicking off in May and critically-acclaimed
musicians
and
shows
coming to our area, there's no better time to stick around than now.
Hotels & Resorts
26. Make a Checklist for Your Pittsburgh Bucket List
We know we threw a lot of things at you, but trust us when we say everything is worth it. Make your own list of what inspires you in our city and hit up as many as you can while in town. And if you don't get to everything this time, we can't wait to see you when you come back.
We Are the City of Champions
Forged by the community. Made for the record books.

title: Work for Visit Pittsburgh | Visit Pittsburgh | Learn how you can join the VisitPITTSBURGH team by viewing our current employment opportunities!
text:
Employment Opportunities
Learn how you can join the VisitPITTSBURGH team by viewing our current openings and learning how to apply.
Who We Are
As the official Destination Marketing Organization (DMO) of Greater Pittsburgh, VisitPITTSBURGH is an Equal Opportunity Employer, employing professionals in the fields of Convention Sales, Sports Development, Destination Services, Marketing, Finance, and Partnership Development. We seek qualified individuals of varied skill sets to fill on-call and full-time career opportunities. VisitPITTSBURGH is a professional workplace environment offering competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.
Recruitment Philosophy, Strategies and Practice
VisitPITTSBURGH annually affirms our equal opportunity policy of non-discrimination against any employee or applicant for employment. Our recruitment philosophy and hiring practices demonstrate an unwavering commitment to equity and diversity. We strive to be a model of welcoming and inclusion, an organization that embraces our differences and welcomes differing opinions and ideas.
VistPITTSBURGH integrates diversity and inclusion practices into our recruitment strategies, and our benchmark is to interview appropriate and qualified candidates. Our standard is to present for each position a diverse pool of candidates.
All applicants and candidates are welcomed and treated with respect and dignity. Qualified applicants are invited to apply for full-time, temporary, and on-call positions. Eligible students are welcome to apply for available internships.
Our employment postings have a wide local, state, and national reach. Applicants apply for open positions via our automated, on-line career portal. Posted positions are pushed out automatically to national job boards like Indeed.
Employment opportunities are shared internally with our staff and Board of Directors, and posted to diverse career websites, such as:
Vibrant Pittsburgh
Indeed
Glass Door
Next Pittsburgh
Imagine Pittsburgh
LinkedIn
Handshake – internships, targeted to undergraduate and graduate students
Pittsburgh Public Relations Society of America
African American Chamber of Commerce
NonProfit Talent
PA Career Link
Veterans Leadership
New Pittsburgh Courier
Destination International
SportsPITTSBURGH, MeetPITTSBURGH and Marketing/Leisure Tourism networks
Recruitment compliance and process:
All processes and employment-related documents are in compliance with federal, state and local laws and regulations including Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Americans with Disabilities Act, Age Discrimination in Employment Act, Equal Pay Act, Fair Credit Reporting Act and Fair Labor Standards Act.
All applications are screened by the Vice President of Human Resources, and shared electronically with the appropriate hiring managers, team members and leadership.
Interviews are conducted with qualified candidates. Interviews include phone and in-person with hiring managers, group interviews with team members and leadership.
In 2012 VisitPITTSBURGH removed the check box from our employment application that asked if an applicant had ever been convicted of a crime. Many states, cities and counties, including the City of Pittsburgh, have passed “Ban-the-Box” legislation. The point of Ban-the-Box laws is to conduct job interviews first, to determine an applicant’s qualifications, before conducting a background investigation and analysis of whether a conviction is job-related.
Assessment testing is provided by a third-party vendor and customized to each position. Our pre-employment assessments are validated for selection during the recruitment process, and assist us by providing data that produces a return on investment.
Background credentialing is managed by a third-party vendor and conducted only when an offer of conditional employment has been extended and the candidate has accepted.

title: Festivals & Cultural Events Marketing Fund | VisitPittsburgh | Visit Pittsburgh | This program aims to support and promote mid-size festivals and cultural events in the Pittsburgh region that drive tourism
text:
Festivals & Cultural Events Marketing Fund
The Festivals & Cultural Events Marketing Fund aims to support and promote mid-size festivals and cultural events in the Pittsburgh region that drive tourism, provide cultural enrichment, and contribute to the city’s vibrant community life.
ELIGIBILITY
SELECTION CRITERIA
SUBMISSION & EVALUATION
APPLICATION
Program Overview
For VisitPITTSBURGH, drivers of the tourism economy are broken into three categories: sports events, business events and leisure tourism. Within leisure tourism, events and festivals are key factors in attracting visitors to the region.
To support the growth and expansion of leisure events in Allegheny County, VisitPITTSBURGH has developed the Festivals & Cultural Events Marketing Fund. This program provides the opportunity for event organizers of Pittsburgh events to apply for, and secure, marketing support from VisitPITTSBURGH.
To be eligible, events must meet the following criteria:
The event must take place in Allegheny County
The event must draw out-of-market visitation and have clear, outlined plans to increase the draw of out-of-market visitation
The event must have a projected attendance of at least 3500 attendees
Events must be ticketed
The event must be a one-day event or take place on concurrent dates
Ex. A three-day festival occurring in one weekend may qualify, but an event series that is broken out over multiple dates throughout a season would not.
Marketing by VisitPITTSBURGH is meant to help existing events grow by increasing the draw of out-of-market visitation. A total of
(4) events
will be selected in 2026 to each receive
marketing support
for this purpose worth
$15,000
.
Events must take place in the year the support is awarded. Additionally,
VisitPITTSBURGH logo recognition and on-site activation opportunities will be required for all events that are awarded funds. Recipients will be required to submit a post-event report to VisitPITTSBURGH no more than 30 days after the event, detailing how the marketing support impacted event attendance.
Events will be evaluated, and events will qualify, based on the review of a completed application and the outcome of VisitPITTSBURGH’s event evaluation process.
The Selection Criteria
Economics
Does the event currently draw out-of-market, overnight visitation to Allegheny County?
Does the event have potential growth for future out-of-market, overnight visitation to Allegheny County?
Awareness
What are the target markets for the event?
Does the event incorporate public relations and/or media engagement opportunities?
Does the event have an established online presence with a website and social media handles?
Does the event have an established social voice?
Community Involvement
Is the event run by a non-profit, charitable organization or a VisitPITTSBURGH business partner?
Does the event involve VisitPITTSBURGH business partners?
Is the event an annual occurrence or a unique, one-time experience?
Marketing
Will the event take place between May 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026?
Can the event or organizing body provide high quality marketing assets?
Does the event have a clear opportunity to be amplified
through VisitPITTSBURGH co-op channels?
Any other points Marketing wants to add?
Submission and Evaluation
VisitPITTSBURGH will accept applications for the 2026 calendar year from
February 10 through March 16
. Applicants may only apply once per year. Events must take place between May 1 and Dec. 31, 2026 to qualify.
Applications should be submitted to
elaine.zedack@visitpittsburgh.com
. Once the application window closes, no further submissions will be accepted. The evaluation process for applications will take up to 30 days after the deadline closes for submissions. During this time, VisitPITTSBURGH may reach out for clarification and additional information.
Upon completion of the evaluation process, VisitPITTSBURGH will award support based on the above criteria.
Please Note: VisitPITTSBURGH’s Festivals & Cultural Events Marketing Fund operates under a policy of nondiscrimination with a steadfast commitment to equity and diversity. VisitPITTSBURGH will not support programs centered on hate speech and/or the unjust or prejudicial treatment of any person or group.
For more information, please contact:
Elaine Zedack, Project Manager, Strategic Initiatives
elaine.zedack@visitpittsburgh.com

title: VisitPittsburgh History | Greater Pittsburgh CVB | Visit Pittsburgh | Go back and read the story of VisitPittsburgh and the Pittsburgh travel industry with historical account going all the way back to the early 1900s.
text:
VisitPITTSBURGH History
​VisitPITTSBURGH is dedicated to generating convention, trade show and leisure travel business for the Pittsburgh region.
Our mission remains intact today as the official tourism promotion agency for Allegheny County and as an independent, nonprofit organization serving its business membership. While it has gone through many changes since it was founded, VisitPITTSBURGH strives to remain true to its mission. The following is a history of this organization that was founded in 1935 to market and serve travelers to Pittsburgh.
Celebrating 90 Years of VisitPITTSBURGH
On June 8, we commemorated the 90th anniversary of VisitPITTSBURGH—a testament to nearly a century of promoting Allegheny County as a premier destination. What began as a small initiative to showcase the city's potential has evolved into a powerhouse of economic impact, generating $6.8 billion for the county and $377 million in state and local tax revenue in 2024, in addition to the 42,600 tourism-supported jobs within the industry. Just as in 1935, our commitment to boosting visitation and fostering economic growth endures.
VisitPITTSBURGH staff and board members gathered to celebrate 90 years.
Throughout our 90-year history, VisitPITTSBURGH demonstrated remarkable resilience, successfully navigating and recovering from major tourism disruptions including 9/11, the 2008 financial crisis, and most recently, the COVID-19 pandemic.
This resilience has paid dividends in measurable ways. Our business and sports events portfolio has generated $1.9 billion in direct visitor spend over the past decade. Business Events has successfully hosted 3,300 conferences and professional events this past decade alone. Nine years ago, we expanded our capabilities with the creation of
SportsPITTSBURGH
, which has already brought signature events to the region, including the National Senior Games (generating $30M+ in economic impact), more than 40 NCAA Championship events and more. This comprehensive track record of success in hosting large-scale events has positioned us perfectly for our next major milestone.
As we enter our tenth decade, we are honored to lead the charge—alongside the Pittsburgh Steelers, and our state, county, and city partners—for the
2026 NFL Draft
. The NFL Draft serves as a catalyst and an introduction to Pittsburgh's capabilities in hosting events of this magnitude, ensuring it will be the first of many more significant events held here in the City of Champions.
The NFL Draft also provides the perfect launch pad for our brand-new leisure marketing campaign. This omnichannel campaign across web, social, digital, print and more will bring the new VisitPITTSBURGH brand to life with a stunning new suite of visuals and compelling storytelling and messaging, designed to capitalize on our unprecedented momentum and national recognition, transforming increased visibility into sustained visitation growth that extends far beyond major events. Leveraging the foundation of excitement from the NFL Draft as well as our recent global recognition, such as via
Lonely Planet's "Best in Travel 2025"
designation as the only US city on their 'must-visit' list, we aim to showcase Pittsburgh like never before—from our world-class museums and burgeoning food and craft beverage scenes to our scenic outdoor spaces and vibrant urban landscapes.
In recent years, Pittsburgh has garnered increased national and international attention—a trajectory we don't anticipate slowing down anytime soon. By staying ahead of industry trends and enhancing visitor experiences across the region, we continue to grow our brand and expand our reach. The rollout of our new marketing campaign over the next year marks another significant goal achieved from our
10-year Tourism Development Plan
.
In 2023, we unveiled our comprehensive 10-Year Tourism Development Plan, a strategic roadmap designed to create enhanced connectivity, add new experiences, and support workforce development opportunities across the tourism industry. The plan encompasses more than 40 strategies and 80 unique action items, forming a blueprint for the development, management, and marketing of tourism assets in both the City of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County. It is crafted with the overall visitor experience in mind, while also identifying ways to enhance the quality of life for residents and those within the local hospitality workforce.
Our Tourism Development Plan builds on decades of efforts to elevate the region's profile, aiming to leave a lasting impression on travelers from near and far. We hope you join us in celebrating these past nine decades of serving the travel and tourism industry in Pittsburgh, as we are enthusiastic about what lies ahead. The city that will surprise you is only just beginning its next chapter!

title: Pittsburgh: From Steel City to Smart City | Visit Pittsburgh | Pittsburgh forges a new future, remaking an iconic steel town into a modern innovation factory.
text:
Technology in Pittsburgh
Pittsburgh forges a new future, remaking an iconic steel town into a modern innovation factory.
Pittsburgh has undergone a dramatic environmental transformation and technological makeover. Pittsburgh ranks among the top cities in the United States for
green certified building space
and is consistently ranked among the
top 10 tech cities
in the country.
Once a center for the production of steel, iron and glass, Pittsburgh is now an advancing leader in aerospace, AI, medicine, education, health care, robotics, software engineering and other tech-forward industries.
Pittsburgh Is Reinventing itself as an Innovation Hub
Next City
Ascender
is a hub for Pittsburgh’s starters and builders, providing programming, insight and connectivity.
Find Out More
Innovation Works
Innovation Works is the largest seed stage investor in the Southwestern Pennsylvania region, and one of the most active in the country.
Find Out More
Pittsburgh's Tech Transformation
To help understand the tech-forward future of Pittsburgh, consider the sleek transformation of the East Liberty neighborhood, where the repurposing of the Nabisco factory into
Google's regional headquarters
symbolizes Pittsburgh's tech-driven resurgence.
Pittsburgh is a city that embraces its history while eagerly embracing the future. Google's presence in East Liberty has significantly contributed to the area's economic growth and technological advancement. With various startups and tech companies establishing a presence in the vicinity, East Liberty has become a hub for innovation, attracting a diverse pool of talent to the area.
Similarly, language-learning platform
Duolingo
, headquartered in Pittsburgh, adds another layer to the city's dynamic landscape. Founded in 2011, Duolingo has grown to become the most popular language-learning app globally, boasting millions of users worldwide. Its commitment to making education accessible has resonated with Pittsburgh's ethos of innovation and progress. Duolingo's success highlights the city's influence in the realm of technology and education, further solidifying its reputation as a multifaceted metropolis that seamlessly integrates its storied past with cutting-edge developments.
Pittsburgh Tech Tourism: How to Enjoy Pittsburgh’s Tech Scene
Pittsburgh has grown into a premiere technology hub, incorporating innovative and high-tech experiences for visitors.
To start, visit Daniel G. and Carole L. Kamin Science Center's
Fab Lab
, a digital fabrication laboratory for innovation and invention, for a unique and educational spin on technology.
Explore the science and history of a real Cold War-era Submarine. Go behind the scenes of the
USS Requin SS 481 Submarine
and take a tech tour into areas rarely seen by the visiting public. See how these amazing vessels and their crew faced life underwater. Explore unrestored compartments, see the conning tower, and check out the periscope.
Older children will love the
Children's Museum
museumlab™, a place where youth eight and older can work with makers to create everything from furniture to apps, experiment with cutting edge technology in the creation of art, climb three stories on a unique sculpture, collaborate on one-of-a-kind art installations and more!
Explore Pittsburgh's history of innovation at the
Duquesne Incline
, the oldest running funicular in the United States. Visitors are able to see the machine room and observe the original hoisting equipment from 1877 that is still in operation today. If that's not enough, the top of the Incline presents you with Pittsburgh's most iconic, must-see view of the city!
Moonshot Museum
Joining the Modern Space Race
Our century-old funiculars are reminiscent of the bygone era, standing in stark contrast to the city's more futuristic endeavors. While the funiculars transport visitors to a time when steel was king, Pittsburgh's role in the space race is a testament to its ceaseless evolution.
Today, the city that once made steel beams now crafts lunar landers, embodying the transition from industrial powerhouse to cutting-edge innovation hub. At the forefront of this transformation are notable companies in the space industry that have set up their operations in Pittsburgh. One such company is
Astrobotic
, a pioneer in commercial lunar exploration, headquartered in the city.
Astrobotic is known for developing lunar payload delivery services and is actively engaged in various lunar missions. Additionally, Space Robotics, a company specializing in advanced robotic systems for space applications, has established a significant presence in Pittsburgh. These companies, along with others in the region, underscore Pittsburgh's transformation into a space technology hub, where the city's industrial past seamlessly integrates with its forward-looking approach to exploring new frontiers in space.
University of Pittsbrugh in Oakland

|
Dave DiCello
Education's Role in Pittsburgh's Technology Scene
Carnegie Mellon University: Home to the first emoticon in 1982, CMU is recognized as one of the first computer science programs in the world and continues to rank as one of the top. The university is known to collaborate with companies such as Apple, Intel, Caterpillar and Disney, helping to expand technology ties in Pittsburgh. Carnegie Mellon University has page after page of
robots
they've created, too.
University of Pittsburgh: Established in 2013, the University of Pittsburgh launched the
Innovation Institute
, a hub innovation and entrepreneurship. The Innovation Institute provides various services for Pitt Innovators including protecting intellectual property, commercializing new discoveries, educational programming and mentoring, and more.

Company that creates high-tech strollers and other baby accessories embedded with robotics and additional patented technology features.
Alphalab:
Software accelerator that helps early-stage tech companies quickly figure out the best way to build and grow in an immersive funding program.

Specializes in tech savvy fishing products; mobile app and online platform that allows users to track and log their fishing trips; developed the AngLR Tracker.
Astrobotic
: From Pittsburgh to the Moon! Astrobotic opened the doors to its new lunar logistics headquarters in Pittsburgh. The 47,000 square foot complex is the largest private facility in the world dedicated to lunar logistics.
Diamond Kinetics:
A sports tech company that created the Swingtracker and Batfitter, two devices designed to enhance the performance of baseball players with extensive performance data.

Online language learning platform; was Apple’s best free iPhone app in 2013.

A national technology news site that provides breaking news, expert analysis and unique insights into the technology industry.
